h1:
Chai Nat Mookata
8 BBQ Grills Worth Your Dinner
intro: Once the sun drops, Chai Nat shifts into grill mode. The smell of marinated pork on the burner drifts down almost every side street. Mookata here is easy on the wallet — plenty of buffets start in the low hundreds, and some places throw in a seat by the Chao Phraya or next to the rice paddies for free. We picked the spots locals actually meet up at, with prices and opening hours so you can plan dinner right away.

blocks.html: Mookata is the dinner Chai Nat locals gather for most — payday, a friend's birthday, or just being hungry and wanting to sit around for a while. The town has everything from cheap buffets in the centre, to riverside spots on the Chao Phraya where the view comes free, out to paddy-side joints in Hankha district that take a bit of a drive but reward you with a nicer setting. We've sorted them by style and price so it's easy to figure out what kind of night you're in the mood for.

Prices listed are rough figures from early 2026. Buffet rates may move up or down by season, and some places charge extra if you leave food on the plate. Worth a quick call before you go if you're a big group or heading out on a long weekend, since the popular spots fill up fast.

blocks.text: The mookata and BBQ spots Chai Nat locals meet at

items.name: Jum Pung Rabert Buffet Mookata
items.blurb: A wallet-friendly buffet that Chai Nat locals talk about a lot. Several styles of marinated pork, seafood, som tam, fried bites, right down to ice cream to finish. Great for rolling in with a group or the family — you can settle in for hours, and it's solid value for what you pay.
items.meta: Phahonyothin Rd, Ban Kluai, Mueang district · open until 22:00

items.name: Riverside Mookata on the Chao Phraya
items.blurb: The draw here is eating right by the Chao Phraya River, with a cool breeze in the evening. The place splits into an à la carte zone, a mookata buffet zone, and a rice-porridge zone, so you choose by mood. The mookata buffet is all-you-can-eat, fresh, and they keep the food coming.
items.meta: On the Chao Phraya riverbank · open 10:00–22:00 (evening buffet)

items.name: Paddy-side Mookata (Hankha district)
items.blurb: A bit of a drive out of town toward Hankha, but plenty of people make the trip for the genuinely chilled-out rice-paddy setting. The dipping sauce has a reputation for being good, it's sold as sets with loads of extra menu items, and it suits a night when you want to escape the bustle in town.
items.price: Sold as sets, from ฿200 per set

items.name: Por Moo Kata, Chai Nat branch
items.blurb: A long-running mookata spot inside Chai Nat town's municipal area, well known to locals. Good burners, strong heat, mild-marinated pork that's easy to eat — a good pick for a weeknight dinner when you don't want to overthink it. Prices are reasonable and parking is easy.
items.price: By set / à la carte, reasonable

items.name: Korean-style BBQ in town
items.blurb: For a night when you want to switch from Thai-style mookata to Korean-style grilling — soy-marinated meat, kimchi side dishes. Spots like this are turning up more often in central Chai Nat. Air-conditioned, good for a relaxed sit-down when you don't want to come home smelling of smoke.

items.name: Night-market stall mookata
items.blurb: Around the night markets and roadsides near the town centre you'll find mookata set up table-by-table along the street. Charged as small sets, good for a quick meal between two or three people with no booking needed. Cheapest on the list, and you get a proper street-side vibe.
items.meta: Night markets / roadsides around town · evening to night

items.name: Mookata by the Chao Phraya Dam
items.blurb: Around the Chao Phraya Dam and the riverbank by Wat Thammamun there are grill spots where you can sit and catch the river breeze. Good after a trip to the dam or evening temple visit, finishing with a mookata meal and a water view. Out-of-towners usually don't know about this one, but Chai Nat locals bring people here often.
items.meta: Near Chao Phraya Dam / Wat Thammamun · evening

items.name: Grill + shabu buffet in town
items.blurb: Some places in town combine mookata and shabu under one roof — pay once and you can grill and boil. Good for a group where everyone wants something different: some want to grill, some want hot pot, all sorted at one table. Works well for a family get-together or a birthday treat.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Most buffet places charge a penalty if you leave food on the plate, especially seafood and beef. Take just enough and go back for more — you'll save money and avoid the extra charge. On Friday and Saturday the popular spots fill up fast, so call to book a table first if you're going as a group.

blocks.text: How to pick the right spot for tonight

blocks.html: Chai Nat mookata comes in a few flavours. Start with what you want out of the night and it gets easier to choose.

items: Cheapest option — go for a buffet in town like Jum Pung Rabert from 129 THB, or a small night-market set from 99 THB.
Want the setting — riverside on the Chao Phraya or paddy-side in Hankha, with a cool breeze and a view. Good for a date or a family night out.
Want air-con and no smoke — pick Korean BBQ in town: clean and comfortable to sit in.
Big group with different tastes — a place that combines grill and shabu sorts everyone at one table, no arguing.

blocks.text: When to go and what to know

blocks.html: Most Chai Nat mookata spots open from late afternoon into the night. Some, like the paddy-side one, open at 15:30, while in-town buffets often run until 22:00. If you want a good riverside table, aim to arrive before 6pm — sunset is when it's busiest.

items: Paying — small spots and roadside stalls are mostly cash. Bring cash and it'll be easier.
Parking — in-town spots have limited parking, while the paddy-side and riverside places have bigger lots.
Smoke — open-air mookata leaves your clothes smelling of smoke. If you'd rather avoid it, pick an air-conditioned spot or one with a smoke-extractor fan.
Evening mosquitoes — paddy-side and riverside spots get mosquitoes after dark. Bring repellent or grab a seat near a fan to be safe.

faq.q: How much does a Chai Nat mookata buffet start at?
faq.a: In-town buffets like Jum Pung Rabert start around 129 THB per person, riverside spots on the Chao Phraya are about 159 THB, and small sets at the night markets start around 99 THB. Prices move with the season, so it's worth a quick call before you go on a long weekend.

faq.q: What time do Chai Nat mookata places open?
faq.a: Most open from late afternoon into the night. The paddy-side spot in Hankha runs about 15:30–22:00, and many in-town buffets go until 22:00. If you want a good riverside table, aim to arrive before 6pm.

faq.q: Which spot is best for riverside mookata in Chai Nat?
faq.a: There's a mookata place right on the Chao Phraya in the town area, with a cool breeze and a water view, plus spots near the Chao Phraya Dam and Wat Thammamun where you can catch the river breeze. Good to combine with a dam visit or an evening temple stop.

faq.q: We're a group with different tastes — which kind of place should we pick?
faq.a: Go for a place that combines mookata and shabu in one. Pay once and you can grill and boil, so whoever wants to grill and whoever wants hot pot is sorted at one table. Works well for a family get-together or a birthday treat.

faq.q: Do Chai Nat mookata buffets charge if you leave food?
faq.a: Plenty of places charge a penalty for leftover food, especially seafood and beef. Best to take just enough and go back for another round — you'll save money and avoid the extra charge.
